primary.title: The Diary of Thomas A. Edison
primary.author: Thomas Edison
primary.rationale: A compilation of Edison's diaries, offering direct insight into his thoughts, experiments, and daily life. While the original diaries are in archives, published versions are likely to be found in digital libraries.

primary.title: Thomas Edison: His Life and Inventions
primary.author: Thomas Edison
primary.rationale: This work, co-authored by Edison himself, provides a biographical account and details of his inventions from his own perspective. It's a foundational primary source for understanding his early career and self-perception.

primary.title: The Papers of Thomas A. Edison
primary.author: Thomas Edison
primary.rationale: A multi-volume collection of Edison's correspondence, laboratory notes, and business records. While extensive, individual volumes or selections might be digitized and available.

secondary.title: Edison: A Biography
secondary.author: Edmund Morris
secondary.rationale: A highly acclaimed and comprehensive biography by a Pulitzer Prize-winning author, offering a scholarly and in-depth analysis of Edison's life and work.

secondary.title: Thomas Edison: The Man Who Illuminated the World
secondary.author: Jill Jonnes
secondary.rationale: A well-researched and engaging biography that places Edison within the broader context of American industrialization and innovation.

secondary.title: The Wizard of Menlo Park: How Thomas Edison Invented the Modern World
secondary.author: Gary B. Kulik
secondary.rationale: This book provides a scholarly examination of Edison's inventive process and his impact on modern society, drawing on extensive archival research.

suggestions.notes: Primary source availability on Project Gutenberg and Wikisource for Edison's own writings can be limited to earlier, less comprehensive works. Internet Archive is a more likely repository for digitized versions of his diaries and collected papers.
